description:
How one portfolio's daily moves line up with four common patterns (the market,
        small versus large companies, value versus growth, momentum), which of
        those sensitivities are distinguishable from zero, and how much of the
        movement the patterns explain.

base.description: Currency every figure is expressed in (USD, EUR, GBP, CAD…). Default USD.
base.title: Base

holdings.description: What is held: {ticker: weight or amount}. Weights need not sum to one; amounts in the base currency are also accepted (then the crises are shown in money). 1 to 100 holdings. Tickers as the exchange lists them (VOO, VWCE.DE, XAW.TO; 'CASH.USD' for cash).
holdings.title: Holdings

name: factor_exposure

outputSchema.description: A four-factor regression of the portfolio's daily returns.

_fence.description: What these figures are and are not: descriptive, no forecast, no advice. Repeat its sense when presenting the result.

alpha_annual.description: Return not explained by the factors, per year (estimated, not a skill measure).

betas.description: Sensitivity per factor: mkt_rf (market), smb (small minus big), hml (value minus growth), mom (momentum).

data.description: Where the prices came from and what was missing or repaired.

as_of.description: Last date of price history used.

missing.description: Tickers with no usable history (left out).

standins.description: Holdings measured through a stand-in with longer history: ticker, proxy, index, from, until, evidence.

fit_caveat.description: Why the fit is poor, when it is.

poor_fit.description: True when the factors explain little.

r_squared.description: Share of the daily movement the factors explain, 0 to 1.

t_stats.description: t-statistic per factor; below about 2 in size, not distinguishable from zero.

title: Sensitivity to common return patterns
